newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate dips to 9.724 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate dips to 9.724 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate slipped to an average of 9.724 percent at the regular weekly auction from 9.804 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The rest of the other maturities also showed declines. The average 182-day T-bill rate dropped to 9.969 from 10.134 percent; and the 364-day rate fell to 10.517 from 10.638 percent.

Traders said the lower T-bill rates were expected since banks continue to experience high liquidity. The auction generated 15.750 billion pesos worth of tenders, of which 4.5 billion pesos were accepted.
A inflow of about 5.0 billion pesos from the maturity of floating rate Treasury notes pulled down rates, they said.
Moreover, banks had been shying away from term reverse repos which carry a 20 percent tax, one dealer said.
Traders said they expected rates to consolidate at current levels unless the Central Bank decides to cut its overnight borrowing rate currently at 10 percent.
